item.title: Iran cannot play role in ensuring security of Bangladesh’s fuel transportation: Ambassador
item.description:
Iran cannot play a direct role in ensuring the security of fuel transportation to Bangladesh or any other country, said Jalil Rahimi jahanabadi, Iran’s ambassador to Bangladesh.

He made the remarks at a press conference held at the Iranian Embassy in Dhaka on Wednesday.

Speaking at the press conference, the Iranian Ambassador claimed that Iran had no involvement whatsoever in the attacks taking place in the Strait of Hormuz.

Jalil Rahimi said that, compromise with the United States and Israel meant surrender.

"Iran will not accept surrender in the name of an agreement," he stated.

Warning of the possibility of a third round of conflict involving nuclear attacks, he cautioned that Iran would retaliate if such an attack took place.

The Iranian ambassador also said that even if US President Donald Trump’s party lost the country’s midterm elections, Washington’s policy on Iran would not change.

He believed that the United States would maintain the same position on Iran regardless of the election results.

Meanwhile, the ambassador expressed satisfaction with the attitude of the people of Bangladesh towards the Iran issue.

He said, "Despite various limitations, the Bangladesh Government’s position on this issue is reasonable."

Jalil Rahimi further said that Iran would never have attacked Middle Eastern countries if the United States had not maintained military bases there.

item.title: Cost of living: Middle class is crumbling; is the state doing well?
item.description:
Last August, the Bangla edition of The Daily Star published the story of a homemaker in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, who used to save Tk 500 a month. In just six months, rising prices of essentials had eroded even that modest capacity to save.

According to Bangladesh Bank, inflation stood at 9.21 per cent in the April-June quarter of this year. In June, incomes rose by 8.2 per cent, while prices increased by 9.2 per cent.

In other words, purchasing power declined despite wage increases. Since the Iran war began in February, the impact of higher oil, gas and electricity prices has been felt in every household. The prime minister has expressed regret over the crisis.

These are signs not so much of poverty as of the fear of slipping further down the economic ladder. American sociologist Barbara Ehrenreich gave this middle-class psychology a name: “fear of falling”. The middle class is less afraid of hunger. Even if someone in this class skips a meal, they will not tell anyone. But the fear of falling one step down the social ladder can keep them awake at night. Today, that ladder is wet and slippery. Many are slipping and falling.

According to a PPRC survey conducted in May 2025, the poverty rate in Bangladesh is around 28 per cent. Another 18 per cent of the population could fall below the poverty line at any time.

According to the World Bank’s updated report of October 2026, around eight million people have fallen into poverty over the past four years, while another 62 million are precariously positioned just above the poverty line.

Many of them belong to the lower-middle class: schoolteachers, small shopkeepers, accountants at private offices and families living in Bangladesh who depend on the earnings of relatives working abroad.

There is a deeply entrenched belief among state policymakers that the poor need help to keep themselves fed, while the rich need help to keep the government in power. The middle class, they assume, will somehow find its own way.

National savings certificates had been the middle class’s last resort. According to Prothom Alo’s calculations, net sales of savings certificates have remained negative for four consecutive years. In February 2026 alone, savings certificates worth more than Tk 11.65 billion were encashed.

Encashing savings certificates means sacrificing the future to meet present needs. Money painstakingly saved for a daughter’s wedding, a father’s medical treatment and one’s own old age is now being consumed to pay for monthly groceries.

2

At least on paper, the poor have social protection. The wealthy have influence. But the middle class has only the obligation to grit its teeth and endure. They feel embarrassed about standing in line at TCB outlets. At the same time, they are afraid to reach for products on supermarket shelves.

Ronald Reagan once joked that the most terrifying sentence in the English language was, “I’m from the government and I’m here to help you.” Much later, documentary filmmaker Michael Moore said in a conversation on the subject, “The government furrows its brows and says, ‘You’re middle class. Why would you need help?’”

There is a deeply entrenched belief among state policymakers that the poor need help to keep themselves fed, while the rich need help to keep the government in power. The middle class, they assume, will somehow find its own way. If they engage in corruption or something of the sort, we will simply turn a blind eye. But corruption is not everyone’s cup of tea. Nor does everyone work in government service.

3

Antonio Gramsci wrote from prison that the old was dying, but the new could not yet be born. This in-between period was dangerous. Bangladesh, too, is stuck in such an interim period. And it is not just the country that is caught between the old and the new; the declining middle class is trapped there as well.

In 2024, this segment of society was among the most optimistic. Now, the gap between expectations and achievements has left it deeply disappointed. It is no longer possible to describe this middle class as a single class; it is better understood as a category. And this category is fragmenting into various subgroups. One such subgroup is the Gen Z middle class.

According to 2022 data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics, around 41 per cent of young people aged 15 to 24 were not engaged in education, employment or training. Among young women, the rate was 62 per cent. More than 28 per cent of graduates from National University-affiliated colleges were completely unemployed.

These statistics also fuelled the anger of Gen Z during the mass uprising of 2024. They managed to change the government, but not their livelihoods or living conditions.

British economist Guy Standing called such declining sections of the middle class “the new dangerous class”. Their jobs are temporary, their incomes uncertain and their futures unclear. They are educated but insecure; angry, anxious and alienated. Out of necessity, they are turning towards populist and extremist politics. Beneath the surface, they are seething, ready to create danger.

A frustrated section of them has become consumed by the idea that they will either leave the country or burn everything down. Both are dangerous thoughts: the first for the country, the second for themselves.

Another section is being forced into the “precariat”. They are taking jobs in Foodpanda, Daraz, Pathao, courier delivery services, online marketplaces, telemarketing, shopping malls, Chinese restaurants and as attendants on long-distance transport.

They may be earning enough to get by from day to day and perhaps just manage to pay their rent. But what about protection? What about the future? They have not even the slightest security.

British economist Guy Standing called such declining sections of the middle class “the new dangerous class”. Their jobs are temporary, their incomes uncertain and their futures unclear.

They are educated but insecure; angry, anxious and alienated. Out of necessity, they are turning towards populist and extremist politics. Beneath the surface, they are seething, ready to create danger.

Another subgroup consists of members of the middle class who have regained a taste of power. Their thinking revolves entirely around demands for “compensation”. Having been deprived of opportunities and privileges for a long time, they now consider it their rightful entitlement to grab every available benefit while the going is good. Statements by ruling party leaders such as “extortion is the responsibility of individuals, not the party” offer this group tacit encouragement.

Another subgroup is the “middle class lying low”. A large number of middle-class people work in offices, banks, universities and government departments who were staunch supporters of the ousted government and remain so. They are now silent in public, speaking only in closed-door gatherings and encrypted groups.

Members of this subgroup first see themselves as “political minorities by circumstance” and then as “social minorities”. This line of thinking is as dangerous as a whirlwind. Concealing such thoughts and allowing resentment to fester is a recipe for disaster.

The “rogue middle class” is the most stable subgroup. Some of its members are officials, contractors, teachers, journalists, editors, physicians, engineers and professional association leaders. They lose no time changing colours. Their objective is to join the ranks of the upper class as quickly as possible. I have given a very small section of this group the name “scarecrow intellectuals”.

They can be seen on television talk shows engaging in verbal battles in defence of the ruling party. It is disappointing when even a university vice-chancellor appears on television as a scarecrow. Some used to call these people the “Justification League”; perhaps now they will be called the “Justification Party”.

4

The cultural decline of the middle-class youth is alarming. The culture of “tagging” and Facebook courts are symptoms of this decline. Trials and verdicts are delivered online. The punishment is “tagging”. It is easy to label someone a Shahbagh supporter, an accomplice of fascists, an Indian agent, pro-Pakistan, an atheist or a fundamentalist.

The question is: how much has our state changed by 2026? Around the world, the condition of the middle class is one of the most important indicators of whether a state is doing well or poorly. If the middle class is doing well, the state is doing well. The middle class is not doing well, and neither is the state.

That is because none of these labels requires any reasoning. Governments change, and the labels change with them. These labels are meaningless, detached from reality and devoid of substance. But their consequences are destructive. Hatred, division, hostility, murderous intent and revenge undermine the cohesion and unity of the state.

Communication through social media can be healthy, but the disorder it can generate is frightening. The ability to communicate through these platforms was one of the main tools behind the fall of the government in 2024. But the resulting disorder is frightening because it deepens divisions among citizens and prolongs misrule.

Moreover, virtual hatred does not remain confined to the virtual world. According to Ain o Salish Kendra, at least 197 people were killed in mob violence in 2025. Before attacks on shrines and sculptures, assaults on homes and similar incidents, incitement is spread on Facebook.

Young people and those in their early twenties are largely responsible. They also take up sticks during mob attacks, write posts and share them. They comment that the victims “got what they deserved”. There is not the slightest sense of guilt.

Recently, a young man named Shamim, who was suffering from a mental health crisis, was murdered after the killing had been announced on Facebook. The person who led the murder showed no remorse. On the contrary, a post in which he boasted about his role gave the impression that there was effectively no government in the country. The law may exist on paper, but it is ineffective.

In psychology, there is an old concept known as the “frustration-aggression theory”. When frustrated people cannot strike at the actual source of their anger, they look for someone weaker to target. You cannot slap market prices or take an electricity bill to court, but you can violently attack someone for their opinions. You can take out your anger on your household cat by kicking it hard because you are angry with your wife.

This cultural decline among the middle class, manifested in the practice of holding online trials on Facebook, began after 2009.

Under Sheikh Hasina’s misrule and authoritarian rule, anyone who took to the streets through legitimate means to protest faced an inevitable fate of enforced disappearance, murder, attacks and lawsuits.

The helpless middle class found an outlet for its anger on social media. The government camp, too, unleashed countless extremist cyber warriors to punish dissenting voices. Obscenity and cyberterrorism were their main weapons.

The question is: how much has our state changed by 2026? Around the world, the condition of the middle class is one of the most important indicators of whether a state is doing well or poorly. If the middle class is doing well, the state is doing well. The middle class is not doing well, and neither is the state.

* Helal Mohiuddin is a Faculty Member, Department of Liberal Arts,

* Mayville State University, North Dakota, USA.

item.title: No clearance without ministry approval to send workers to Russia, 11 other countries
item.description:
The government has tightened monitoring to prevent human trafficking, making approval from the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment mandatory for sending workers to 12 countries, including Russia.

The ministry has instructed authorities not to issue clearances without its prior approval.

The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare issued the directive in a letter sent to the Director General of the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) on Wednesday.

According to the letter, instructions were given not to issue immigration clearances for workers bound for Serbia, Moldova, Belarus, the Republic of the Congo, Russia, Japan, Iraq, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Ukraine, and Libya without recruitment permission or formal approval from the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment.

On the same day, the Bangladesh Association of International Recruiting Agencies (BAIRA) notified all its member agencies regarding the decision.

BAIRA circulated the instruction after receiving the ministry’s letter to alert its members, attaching a copy of the official directive.

Industry insiders say ministry approval was previously not required for recruitment demand letters covering up to seven workers. There have been allegations that this provision was misused to send workers abroad using fake job offers.

Under the new directive, approval must be obtained for every recruitment demand letter before workers can be sent abroad. This is expected to enhance monitoring and accountability.

Sector insiders say Bangladeshi workers seeking employment in these 12 countries must refrain from engaging in financial transactions or making final decisions before verifying their appointment letters, ministerial approvals and immigration clearances.

Volunteers from several organisations involved in the migration process say that obtaining a visa or receiving a job offer through a recruiting agency does not, by itself, guarantee legal and safe migration. It is important to verify the actual employment opportunities in the destination country, the identity of the employer, the employment contract, salary and benefits, the type of visa and approval from the relevant authorities in Bangladesh.

Volunteers from several migration rights organisations stressed that merely securing a visa or receiving a job offer through a recruiting agency does not guarantee legal and safe migration.

They noted that it is critical to verify genuine employment prospects in the destination country, the employer’s credentials, employment contracts, wage structures, visa categories, and valid government approvals from Bangladesh.

They added that developments in countries such as Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam—where individuals are forcibly detained in online scam compounds and coerced into cyber fraud—have triggered widespread international concern.

Many Bangladeshis who travelled to these countries after being promised jobs have fallen victim to fraud, exploitation, confinement and human trafficking. As a result, extra caution is necessary when considering employment offers in these destinations. Many people are also becoming involved in the war after travelling to Russia.

item.title: Pori Moni granted bail on Tk 500 bond
item.description:
Actress Pori Moni has been granted bail after surrendering before a court in a case filed by businessman Nasir Uddin Mahmud over allegations of assault, vandalism and intimidation. The court granted her bail today, Thursday, a day after issuing an arrest warrant against her.

Pori Moni got out of a white car parked on the premises of the Dhaka Chief Judicial Magistrate Court at 11:40 am today. She appeared before the court and surrendered at 11:55 am, seeking bail. After a hearing, Judicial Magistrate Mahfuzur Rahman granted her bail on a bond of Tk 500.

Her lawyer, Nilanjona Rifat, confirmed the matter to Prothom Alo. She said, “The court issued an arrest warrant against Pori Moni yesterday. We surrendered before the court today and applied for bail. After the hearing, the court granted her bail.”

Wednesday was scheduled for the recording of witness testimony in the case. However, Pori Moni could not appear before the court.

Although her lawyer filed an application seeking more time on her behalf, the court rejected it, cancelled her bail and ordered the issuance of an arrest warrant.

Nasir Uddin Mahmud filed the case at a Dhaka court on 6 July 2022. In his complaint, he alleged that on the night of 9 June 2021, Pori Moni and her associates went to the Boat Club in Savar. At around 1:15 am, as he and his associate Shah Shahidul Alam were leaving the club, Pori Moni called him over and asked him to sit with her for a while.

Nasir alleged that at one point, Pori Moni pressured him to give her a bottle of alcohol free of charge. When he refused, she verbally abused him. During an ensuing altercation, she threw a glass and a mobile phone at him, injuring his head and chest. In the case, Nasir also accused her of assault, threatening to kill him and vandalising the club.

Meanwhile, Pori Moni had earlier filed a case at Savar Police Station against Nasir Uddin and others over the Boat Club incident, accusing them of rape and attempted murder.

The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) submitted its investigation report to the court in 2024. In the report, investigation officer and PBI Dhaka District Inspector Md Monir Hossain said evidence had been found to support the allegations of assault and intimidation against Pori Moni and her costume designer, Junaid Bogdadi Jimi. However, the report stated that no evidence had been found to support the allegations against another accused, Fatema Tuz Jannat Bony.

After accepting the investigation report, the court issued summonses directing Pori Moni and Jimi to appear before it. They appeared in court and secured bail on 25 June 2024.

item.title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
item.description:
A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say.

Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump's maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing:

Will tariffs be limited

Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump's liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say.

That could be a potential blow to Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January.

If Democrats limit Trump, that means he "will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China", said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai.

However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump's tariffs among US businesses.

Congress will "take every opportunity to thwart (Trump's policies) over the next two years", said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore's Nanyang Technological University.

But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that "are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses... who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats", Thompson said.

Congress will be "less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict", said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington.

Taiwan a 'game changer'?

The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a "game changer", said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics.

Washington is Taipei's most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars' worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack.

But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons.

China could use the remaining two years of Trump's presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing "judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene", Shearing wrote in a note.

Trump, who recently hailed his "great friendship" with China's President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats -- and some Republican lawmakers -- to greenlight the arms package.

But a Democrat-controlled Congress "may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year", Wu said.

"If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship."

Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be "a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan", said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute.

Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it "or simply ignore it".

Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck?

From China's perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say.

"Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington," said Kim.

"Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations," she added.

Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said "Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him".

But, he added, Beijing is "calculating" and "would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly"

item.title: Taskin strikes twice as West Indies reach 86-3 at lunch
item.description:
Bangladesh made an encouraging start with the ball, taking three West Indies wickets in the opening session of the Sylhet Test, but a fourth-wicket partnership helped the visitors recover to 86-3 at lunch in the second Test.

West Indies, who elected to bat after winning the toss  at Sylhet International Stadium on Thursday, were reduced to 27-3 before Amir Jangoo and Test debutant Kevin Wickham steadied the innings with an unbeaten 59-run stand.

Jangoo was batting on 32 and Wickham on 27 at the interval, with the visitors reaching 86 in 26 overs.

Taskin Ahmed led Bangladesh's attack with two wickets, while Hasan Mahmud claimed the other. Taskin made the first breakthrough by bowling opener Brandon King for nine with a full-length delivery that swung in and continued to move after pitching.

Hasan then dismissed Kavem Hodge with a delivery that skidded through and hit the middle stump. Taskin struck again, trapping Joshua Da Silva leg-before for 12 to leave West Indies struggling at 28-3.

Bangladesh had an early opportunity to strike when Da Silva offered a straightforward catch to Shadman Islam to slip off Hasan's bowling, but the fielder failed to hold on.

Jangoo and Wickham capitalised on the reprieve, batting cautiously to take West Indies to lunch without further loss.

Wickham, West Indies' 349th Test cricketer, made an impressive entry into international cricket. The Barbados batter had scored three consecutive centuries in his last three innings in the West Indies Championship in April and May, making 105, 153 and an unbeaten 108. He finished the competition with 393 runs at an average of 78.60, the third-highest aggregate.

He also has a strong first-class record, scoring six centuries in 25 matches at an average of 40.88.

Taskin and Hasan bowled for much of the opening session and appeared to be feeling the strain towards the end. Bangladesh's spin duo of Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Taijul Islam bowled a combined 10 overs but failed to take a wicket.

Bangladesh retained their combination of three spinners and two pacers for the second Test, with Taskin replacing Shoriful Islam. Mushfiqur Rahim also returned to the side after missing the Mirpur Test through injury.

The Sylhet weather was overcast throughout the morning, with a slight chill in the air.

West Indies 86-3 at lunch (26 overs): Amir Jangoo 32, Kevin Wickham 27, Joshua Da Silva 12, Brandon King 9; Taskin Ahmed 2-36, Hasan Mahmud 1-33, Mehidy Hasan Miraz 0-13, Taijul Islam 0-3.

item.title: Tax on savings certificates no longer final, who benefits and who loses
item.description:
In the budget for the current fiscal year, The withholding tax deducted from profits earned on savings certificates has been excluded from the list of final taxes.

This means that when purchasing savings certificates, a 10 per cent tax is deducted from the profit earned. If an investor does not possess a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), a 15 per cent tax is deducted from the profit.

Until now, this tax was considered final. No additional tax had to be paid on profits from savings certificates. Once deducted, the tax could not be reclaimed either.

However, starting from the current fiscal year, the tax deducted at source on the profit of savings certificates will no longer be considered a final tax liability. It will instead be treated as an advance tax.

If excess tax is deducted by year-end, the surplus amount can be claimed as a refund. Conversely, if the calculated liability is higher, the remaining amount must be paid to the tax department of the National Board of Revenue (NBR). These calculations are made through income tax returns.

Let us look at who stands to benefit and who may lose under the new rule.

What has changed

The withholding tax deducted when profits from savings certificates are paid will no longer be considered the final tax liability. From now on, income from savings certificates will be added to a taxpayer's total income and tax will be charged according to the applicable tax slabs for each individual.

Who benefits and who loses

Every taxpayer is required to pay taxes at rates of 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 per cent at year end based on their income (if it exceeds the tax-free threshold). As a result of this new rule, taxpayers who fall into tax slabs higher than 10 per cent will see an increase in their tax burden. This is because the 10 per cent tax previously deducted at source was considered final and served as an exemption from further tax liabilities.

Consider an example. A taxpayer earns Tk 100,000 in profit from savings certificates in a year. A total of Tk 10,000 is deducted as withholding tax. The taxpayer also earns another Tk 350,000 from salaries or other sources. This brings the total taxable income to Tk 450,000. No tax is payable on the first Tk 400,000, while the remaining Tk 50,000 is taxed at 10 per cent, amounting to Tk 5,000.

However, since the taxpayer has already paid Tk 10,000 as advance tax on the savings certificates, they can claim a refund for the remaining Tk 5,000 when filing the tax return.

This will benefit low-income and middle-class families who rely heavily on profits from savings certificates, reducing their tax burden. If excess tax has been deducted, they will receive a refund.

Under the new system, taxpayers whose applicable tax rates are higher than 10 per cent will have to pay tax on that income according to their actual tax slabs, such as 15 per cent, 20 per cent or higher.

Here is another example. A taxpayer earns Tk 500,000 in profit from savings certificates. At a withholding tax rate of 10 per cent, Tk 50,000 is deducted. The taxpayer also earns Tk 400,000 from a salary or other sources. This brings their total annual income to Tk 900,000.

Under the previous system, the taxpayer would have had to pay only Tk 50,000 in tax, as the tax paid on savings certificate profits was considered final. Under the new system, however, the calculation will be as follows: no tax on the first Tk 400,000; 10 per cent tax on the next Tk 300,000, amounting to Tk 30,000; and 15 per cent tax on the following Tk 200,000, amounting to another Tk 30,000.

The taxpayer's total tax liability will therefore be Tk 60,000. Since Tk 50,000 has already been paid as withholding tax on savings certificate profits, the taxpayer will have to pay an additional Tk 10,000. This will be the extra tax payable for the year.

How to claim an advance tax refund

If the amount deducted as tax is higher than the taxpayer's actual tax liability, the excess can be refunded.

For example, Tk 30,000 may be deducted as advance tax on a taxpayer's savings certificate profits over the course of a year. But when filing the annual return, the taxpayer may find that their total tax liability is Tk 20,000 after accounting for various tax rebates. In that case, the remaining Tk 10,000 can be refunded.

To receive a refund of advance tax deducted from savings certificate profits, taxpayers must file an income tax return. Therefore, people who make small investments in savings certificates but have no taxable income will now need to obtain a TIN and file an annual return to reclaim the advance tax deducted from their profits.

When filing the return, taxpayers must provide their bank account number and claim the refund. They must also submit documents as proof of the tax deducted at source. After verification, tax officials will refund the amount due to the taxpayer's bank account within 120 days.

item.title: 4 people burned in gas cylinder leak fire in Gazipur
item.description:
Four people sustained burn injuries when a fire broke out following a gas cylinder leak in the Naojor area of Gazipur. One of them is in critical condition. The injured are receiving treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery.

The fire broke out at United Cylinder Re-testing Centre-2, next to Riaz Filling Station in the Naojor area of Gazipur city, at around 8:30 pm on Wednesday.

Talha Bin Jasim, a member of the media cell of the Fire Service and Civil Defence, said 18-year-old Abdullah suffered burns to 20 per cent of his body, 19-year-old Ahad to 55 per cent, 26-year-old Ashraful to 15 per cent and 25-year-old Naim to 4 per cent.

According to the Fire Service, flames engulfed 41 cylinders at the centre. Two Fire Service units reached the scene at 8:44 pm after receiving the report. Firefighters brought the blaze under control at around 9:30 pm. Initial assessments suggest that gas leaked from a filled cylinder, causing the accident.

Talha Bin Jasim said hospital authorities had admitted Abdullah and Ahad to the High Dependency Unit (HDU). Naim remains under observation in the emergency department. He added, "Ahad is in critical condition as 55 per cent of his body has suffered burns." The injured are receiving treatment.

item.title: New wage structure for garment workers to take effect in December
item.description:
A new wage structure for workers in the ready-made garment industry will come into effect in December. Garment workers will receive their increased salaries from January. Representatives of workers and employers agreed on this at the first meeting of the Minimum Wage Board.

The representatives disclosed the information to journalists after a meeting held yesterday, Wednesday, at the Minimum Wage Board office in Segunbagicha, Dhaka, to revise wages for garment workers. The meeting was chaired by the board’s new chairman, Syed Azad Subhani, who took office yesterday.

The meeting began shortly after 11:00 am. Among those who attended in person were ABM Shamsuddin, director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), representing employers; Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Industrial Workers Federation (BGIWF), representing workers; Anwar Hossain, president of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal and a permanent worker representative on the board; and Asif Ayub, joint secretary-general of the Bangladesh Employers’ Federation and permanent employer representative. The neutral member, Dhaka University professor Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, joined the meeting online.

After the meeting, Minimum Wage Board Chairman Syed Azad Subhani told journalists, “At the first meeting, we briefed everyone on the process of determining wages. At the board’s next meeting next week, the employer and worker representatives will submit their wage proposals in writing.”

Worker representative Babul Akhter said the employer representatives had agreed that the new wages would take effect in December so that workers could receive their increased salaries in January. He added, “At the meeting, we requested the neutral member of the wage board to submit a wage proposal. We hope the neutral member will also put forward a proposal.”

Babul Akhter said, “Workers have many grievances and complaints, as well as resentment. We will address these issues gradually. We urge the government to implement labour laws.”

Addressing workers, he also said that third parties were involved in the ongoing wage movement and urged them to remain neutral and refrain from illegal activities. He demanded the immediate release of workers and labour leaders who had been arrested.

Employer representative ABM Shamsuddin said, “We are committed to completing this process by December so that workers can receive the new wages from January. We have no disagreement on this.”

Following protests by workers, the Labour Ministry formed the wage board last Sunday. However, the protests have continued despite its formation. Workers also demonstrated yesterday in Gazipur, Savar, Mirpur and Narayanganj. As a result, production was disrupted at 492 garment factories. Of these, 92 factories announced closures for one, two or three days.

Asked about the situation, BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan told Prothom Alo last night, “There has been no improvement in the protest situation in the industrial areas. The situation today (Wednesday) was much the same as on Tuesday. Production has been disrupted at many factories. The first meeting of the wage board has taken place. We hope the situation will improve from tomorrow (today).”

Wage board chairman replaced

Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, a district and sessions judge, had taken office as chairman of the wage board last September. The chairman was replaced yesterday morning, before the board’s first meeting.

In a notification issued by the Law and Justice Division of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman was transferred to the post of director (training) at the Judicial Administration Training Institute.

The same order appointed Syed Azad Subhani, a judge of the Pirojpur Tribunal for the Prevention of Child Violence and a district and sessions judge, as the new chairman of the wage board.

However, the notification did not state any reason for removing Ashfaqur Rahman. Multiple sources said the government had been unable to place its confidence in the outgoing chairman to determine wages in a sensitive sector such as the garment industry.

Workers urged to return to work

A tripartite meeting involving workers, employers and the government was held yesterday evening at the Labour Ministry in the Secretariat. Labour Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury chaired the meeting.

Those present included Mahdi Amin, the prime minister’s adviser on labour and employment; Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas, chairman of the parliamentary standing committee on labour and employment and a labour leader; BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan; BKMEA President Mohammad Hatem; and labour leaders Montu Ghosh, Nazma Akter and Taslima Akter, among others.

At a press conference after the meeting, Labour Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said, “We have formed a new wage board within three years in the shortest possible time. Through impartial discussions, this board will announce a reasonable and fair minimum wage by December.”

He urged workers to return to their factories voluntarily and peacefully.

The labour minister said that, on behalf of the prime minister, an initial financial assistance of Tk 100,000 had been provided through the local administration to the family of Toufiq Hossain, a worker killed during the labour protests in Gazipur.

He added that the relevant authorities had been instructed to bring those involved in the killing to justice swiftly.

Mahdi Amin said an acceptable and fair minimum wage for garment workers would be announced by December.

He further said some outsiders were entering peaceful gatherings of ordinary workers and inciting them, creating tension and engaging in violence and sabotage. Ordinary workers were not involved in such misdeeds, he added.

The ;aw enforcement agencies would handle the situation with the utmost sincerity and patience and ensure justice, Mahdi Amin added.

item.title: Trump’s midterm drubbing demonstrates the power of data centre opponents
item.description:
USA-ELECTION/CALIFORNIA

  • Democrats promising data center moratoriums win state offices

  • AI stocks drop as opponents are set to take political power

  • Goldman says 45pc of planned US data center capacity at risk

Data center opponents were among the biggest winners of the Democrats’ landslide victories in the US midterm elections, pointing to a shifting public mood on AI and, investors said, a possible slowdown of the boom that has propelled US economic growth and stock markets.

The size and breadth of the Democratic wave were still coming into focus on Wednesday. But in gubernatorial races in Texas and Georgia, Democrats who campaigned in part on a moratorium on data center development won offices that the party has not held for decades.

Their victories hand political heft to opponents of the projects, which are at the heart of the AI boom but are loud, thirsty for water, hungry for electricity and increasingly unpopular with their neighbours, investors said.

US-based data center stocks slid as the Democratic sweep became apparent. Core Scientific fell 11.6 per cent and Iren tumbled 12.5 per cent, while other AI infrastructure firms such as Applied Digital, Hut 8 Corp, Cipher Digital and power firms such as GE Vernova, Constellation Energy and Vistra slumped.

Investors said the results are likely to usher in tougher regulation and could ripple across financial markets where AI stocks were falling on Wednesday; big bets have already started to wobble due to concerns about spending and overcapacity.

“In our view, the significance of these midterm elections is more like a referendum on AI than a referendum on (Donald) Trump,” said Aidan Yao, a senior investment strategist at the Amundi Investment Institute, the research arm of Europe’s largest asset manager.

“If the AI theme is subject to some restrictions, then the US economy, US inflation and US monetary policy all become very, very uncertain.”

In the mix too is the upcoming IPO of Anthropic, which is preparing to begin formally marketing shares to prospective investors next week. An amended regulatory filing on Monday showed Anthropic’s net loss narrowed in the third quarter, as revenue surged 47 per cent from a quarter earlier to $16.96 billion, though the pace of growth slowed.

Texas sweep

The most stunning ballot box repudiation was in Texas, which GLJ Research has estimated accounts for about a quarter of US data center capacity due to come online by 2030.

But Democrat Gina Hinojosa ousted Greg Abbott as governor in an upset that ended three decades of Republican hold on the office, while fellow party member James Talarico became the senator-elect.

A conservative, oil-producing state, Texas has worked for years to reinvent itself as a tech hub, attracting companies such as SpaceX SPCX.O and entrepreneurs like Elon Musk, who donated more than $150 million to Ken Paxton, the Republican who lost to Talarico.

But even Republicans turned against data centers, which opponents say drive up utility bills, pollute the night sky with lights and do not create sufficient jobs or taxes to justify the incentives that states pay.

“Data centres in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk said on social media after the election.

Goldman Sachs said Democratic victories at the state and local level would likely lead to temporary halts to projects, potentially affecting some 45 per cent of planned US data centre capacity expansion, though they think it will be short-lived.

In Georgia, where commercial real estate services and investment firm CBRE says Atlanta is the most active data center construction market in the country, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won the gubernatorial contest, ending more than two decades of Republican control.

How widely the data center and AI business is affected remains to be seen, HSBC analysts Max Kettner and Duncan Toms wrote.

“One possible – and entirely feasible – scenario is that we won’t see broad-based data center moratoriums but rather more regulations/higher oversight on data centers,” they said. “Another one is that data centers simply move from Texas to other states.”

Analysts at Morgan Stanley said the election of Democrat Amy Acton in Ohio as governor creates a significant risk of data center project delays in that state, including a 10-gigawatt project involving Nvidia NVDA.O that is the largest in the state. Ohio put a moratorium earlier this year on considering new data center tax exemption requests.

The AI trade

AI growth has driven stocks higher this year due to bets on chip demand while pushing up bond yields, as the data center construction boom boosts economic growth.

Chip and AI firms like TSMC, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Kioxia fell in Asia – along with bond yields – on Wednesday.

To be sure, many analysts said a slowdown in the building of data centers in the US did not necessarily herald a change in demand for AI or computing power, and some view a roughly 8 per cent drawdown in the Nasdaq .IXIC over the past month as an opportunity to buy.

Tommaso Leodari, Dubai-based chief investment officer of hedge fund Index & Cie, said the risks for data centers were difficult to predict, given their vital role in America’s competition with China.

“I do not foresee limitations, higher taxes, or other kinds of opposition to the force behind a new industrial revolution for the US. I consider that Dems are going to continue being more moderate than before, so any fury will be directed at Trump and his team, not at a new industry that can save American imperialism,” he said.

item.title: 9th teacher recruitment exam: NTRCA gives timeline
item.description:
The 9th teacher recruitment examination under the Non-Government Teachers’ Registration and Certification Authority (NTRCA) may be held in December.

The plan is to organise the examination after the ongoing viva voce examinations for the recruitment of heads and assistant heads of educational institutions are completed.

According to NTRCA sources, the viva voce examinations for the recruitment of heads and assistant heads of educational institutions are currently underway and are scheduled to end on 9 December. The 9th teacher recruitment examination may be held afterwards. However, a final decision on the examination will be taken only after approval from the Ministry of Education.

There will be a major change in the recruitment process this time. For the first time, the registration examination will lead directly to recruitment rather than merely assessing candidates’ eligibility. As a result, it will be called the 9th teacher recruitment examination instead of the 19th teacher registration examination, following the previous numbering sequence.

The last notice for the 18th teacher registration examination was published on 4 November 2023. The preliminary examination was held in March 2024, around four months later. After a prolonged gap, a new teacher recruitment examination is now being planned.

item.title: Army soldier killed in gunfight during anti-trafficking operation in Teknaf
item.description:
An army soldier was killed in an exchange of fire between joint forces and an armed human trafficking gang during an operation to rescue hostages in Rongikhali hills of Teknaf upazila, Cox’s Bazar, on Thursday.
Acting on intelligence, a joint team comprising members of the Bangladesh Army’s 10 Infantry Division, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and local police launched the operation at around 5pm on November 5.
According to an ISPR, an armed gang of 15–16 members had held approximately 120 Rohingya and Bangladeshi nationals hostage in the remote hilly area.
The gang members opened fire after sensing the presence of the joint forces, triggering an exchange of gunfire between the 2 sides.
During the exchange, Army soldier Md Titas Sheikh, 27, was shot in the left shoulder and sustained severe blood loss.
He was rescued and given initial treatment at a nearby hospital before being transferred to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Ramu for advanced treatment, where the attending physician declared him dead.
During the operation, the joint forces recovered 1 pistol, 1 locally made firearm and 4 rounds of ammunition. They also detained 5 suspected members of the gang and rescued 57 hostages.
The Bangladesh Army expressed deep condolences to the deceased soldier’s family and paid tribute to his sacrifice while performing his duties.

item.title: NBR orders bank account freezing of 100 suspected individuals
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has directed banks and financial institutions to freeze the bank accounts of approximately 100 individuals suspected of being involved in instigating unrest in the ready-made garment (RMG) industry.
For the same reason, the agency has also requested detailed bank transaction information for another 125 entities.
This initiative has been undertaken to investigate whether funds belonging to these individuals and organizations were used to finance instability within the garment sector.
This information was obtained from NBR sources, who stated that two intelligence units of the NBR sent letters to banks and financial institutions requesting them to identify and freeze the bank accounts of these individuals.
Additionally, the agency has asked for detailed transaction statements for the 125 entities.
Most of the individuals on the list are associated with the ousted Awami League government.
They include former ministers, members of parliament, and influential business leaders.
Notable individuals on the list feature Salman F Rahman, Abdus Salam Murshedy, Tipu Munshi, Shahriar Alam, Nasrul Hamid, and Tajul Islam.
Furthermore, business figures named on the list include Fazlur Rahman of Tusuka Group, Abdus Salam of Well Group, Khosru Chowdhury of Nipa Group, Mosharraf Hossain of Standard Group, and SM Mannan Kochi, former president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA).
The names of their family members are also included.
According to NBR sources, the list of individuals whose accounts are being frozen also includes Alif Molla, brother-in-law of cricketer Shakib Al Hasan.
Sources further stated that evidence of transactions conducted via cryptocurrencies, in addition to mobile financial services, has been uncovered.
A senior NBR official, speaking on condition of anonymity, stated that the initiative to identify and freeze the bank accounts was taken based on information provided by several government agencies. At the same time, transaction statements for a large number of institutions have been requested.
Asked about the reason, the official explained that these individuals and entities are accused of financing activities aimed at creating unrest in the garment industry.
Their financial transactions are being scrutinized to verify the truth of these allegations.
Some of these individuals are currently in prison, while others are in hiding. However, the NBR's investigation into the allegations against them has not yet concluded.
Officials concerned noted that this list could grow even longer, describing the investigation as an ongoing process.
They were unable to specify when the probe would reach completion.

item.title: Art Dhaka holds special preview before public opening on Nov 6
item.description:
Bringing together the diverse worlds of art, architecture, performance and cultural expression, Art Dhaka is set to open its doors to the public on Friday at Aloki in the capital, offering a five-day celebration of creativity and artistic exchange. The fair will welcome visitors daily from 10 am to 10 pm until November 10.
Ahead of its public opening, Art Dhaka hosted a special preview on Thursday, welcoming an impressive gathering of invited guests, including ambassadors of various countries, renowned artists from different creative sectors, cultural and entertainment personalities, business figures, art enthusiasts and collectors.
Founded by Durjoy Rahman, Nahar Khan, Fahd Sattar and Aumia Khundkar, Art Dhaka brings together their experience in art, culture, media and creative industries to establish a platform for artistic expression, cultural exchange and engagement with the wider creative community.
The main art fair features two curated sections: 'The Still Point' on the upper floor, curated by Najmun Nahar Keya, and 'Narration. Thought. Chronicles.' on the ground floor, curated by Zihan Karim. Artworks on display will be available for purchase by visitors and collectors.
Highlighting the distinctive processes and traditions of printmaking, the Print Pavilion, titled 'The Art of Access' and curated by Fareha Zeba, brings together prints and works on paper by artists from different generations, offering visitors an accessible entry point into art collecting.
Beyond the main fair, Art Dhaka features several specially conceived exhibitions and installations. 'Leaping Across Time', curated by Mustafa Zaman, pays tribute to pioneering artists whose practices laid the foundations of modern art in Bangladesh.
The Immersive Art Zone offers new ways of experiencing artistic legacies through images, sound, movement and spatial storytelling, featuring works and visual worlds of major Bangladeshi artists, including Zainul Abedin and SM Sultan. It also presents a specially developed showcase of works from Bangladeshi artist Rokeya Sultana's 'Fata Morgana' series.
The Pavilion, located in the parking area, features an architectural intervention designed by architect Rashed Chowdhury, drawing inspiration from Bengal's architectural heritage and material traditions. Its sustainable construction approach allows materials and components to be dismantled, repurposed and reused after the event, while the space will also accommodate art installations and interactive works.
The Glasshouse will host talks, panel discussions, artist conversations and performative arts, bringing together artists, architects, curators, collectors and cultural practitioners to discuss contemporary art and creative practices.
Shala, the Collector's Lounge, will provide an intimate setting for artists, collectors and invited guests to interact. A curated food outlet will offer traditional Bangladeshi flavours in contemporary formats, while the Art Dhaka Shop in the lobby will feature event merchandise, artist-led products, publications, digital print editions and design objects.
Together, these spaces position Art Dhaka as a broader cultural platform where art can be viewed, experienced, discussed and collected, with architecture, sustainability, performance, food and design forming integral parts of the experience.

item.title: DB arrests 8 more over attack on police in Mirpur
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested 8 more people over an attack on police personnel during a garment workers' protest in Mirpur, Dhaka, which left several officers seriously injured.
On Thursday, Deputy Commissioner of the DMP Media and Public Relations Division Md Akhtar Hossain said a group of troublemakers posing as protesters surrounded police personnel on duty and launched a sudden attack in the Mirpur-11 area last Tuesday.
The attackers beat the officers with sticks and large pieces of bricks, leaving several police personnel seriously injured.
At around 9am that day, garment workers blocked the road and staged a protest in Mirpur-11. When police attempted to clear the road and bring the situation under control, clashes broke out.
Some individuals among the protesters began throwing bricks and stones at police. Officers responded by firing sound grenades and tear gas shells, followed by repeated chases and counter-chases between the 2 sides.
During the clashes, the attackers surrounded and beat several police personnel after isolating them.
The DB identified those involved by reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and using technological assistance before arresting them.

item.title: Tahsif Sauri death: Dip gets fresh 3-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court has granted a third spell of remand, this time for three days, for Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip in a murder case filed over the death of former air force officer KM Tahsif Sauri.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Monirul Islam passed the order on Thursday following a petition by the investigation officer. State lawyer Muhammad Shamsuddoha Sumon confirmed the development.
Inspector Firoz Uddin of the Tongi River Police Outpost, the investigation officer, had sought seven days’ remand, citing five reasons. These included establishing the motive behind the alleged killing, recovering evidence, identifying the suspected mastermind and accomplices, checking Dip’s statements against eyewitness accounts and CCTV footage, and understanding how the incident took place.
Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruqui argued in favour of the remand, while Dip’s lawyer, Monirul Islam, sought his release on bail and opposed further questioning. After hearing both sides, the court granted three days’ remand.
Tahsif’s body was recovered by river police from the Rajabari Ghat area of the Turag River on the afternoon of October 28. He had left home on his motorcycle on the evening of October 27 after Dip called him downstairs.
Dip said on October 29 that he had dinner with Tahsif at a restaurant before parting ways in the Uttara House Building area. He was handed over to river police on the night of October 30, amid discussions over what action would be taken against him after no case had been filed within three days of the body’s recovery.
After Tahsif’s father filed the case that night, police showed Dip arrested. He was initially remanded for four days, followed by a second three-day remand on Tuesday.
Police recovered Tahsif’s motorcycle from Tongi’s Mazar slum area on the morning of October 30, based on information provided by Dip. He also admitted to visiting the area with Tahsif late at night. Investigators from the Police Bureau of Investigation later visited the area with him.
Dip is described in the case as a close acquaintance of Tahsif. The former air force officer had drawn attention for allegedly recording a video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country.
Meanwhile, Tahsif’s girlfriend, Jerika Tasnim Disha, was placed on a second three-day remand on Wednesday after an initial four-day spell. She was reportedly seen with Tahsif at a bar in Uttara on the night of the incident.

item.title: Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury sent to jail in murder case; no bail sought
item.description:
A Dhaka court has ordered former information adviser to ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and DBC News Chairman Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury to be sent to jail in a case filed over the killing of madrasa student Md Arif in Jatrabari during the July uprising.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque passed the order on Thursday following a petition filed by the investigation officer, said public prosecutor Muhammad Shamsuddoha Chowdhury.
Sub-Inspector Mohammad Amir Hossain of Jatrabari police station and also the investigation officer of the case sought an order to keep Iqbal Sobhan in jail.
Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury's lawyer Chowdhury Mohammad Galib Ragib did not seek bail but requested proper medical treatment and division facilities for his client.
He told the court that Iqbal Sobhan is a senior journalist and CEO of DBC News who suffers from diabetes, high blood pressure and neurological complications. He requested the court to ensure that his client receives division facilities and proper medical care in jail.
During the hearing, Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi outlined the allegations against Iqbal Sobhan.
He alleged that Iqbal Sobhan secured ownership of DBC News by pleasing Sheikh Hasina and was subsequently appointed her information adviser. In that capacity, he allegedly facilitated the issuance of television licences and exercised control over the media.
The prosecutor further alleged that the former adviser took steps to prevent protesters' statements from being broadcast during the July uprising. He also accused him of forming an organisation with journalist Mozammel Haque Babu and bringing television channels under government control.
Faruqui claimed that Iqbal Sobhan amassed considerable wealth in the Gulshan and Banani areas through these activities before going into hiding following the fall of the Hasina government. Law enforcement agencies arrested him on Wednesday, he added.
The defence lawyer Chowdhury Mohammad Galib Ragib said Iqbal Sobhan had served as the former prime minister's information adviser, a position equivalent in rank to a state minister, and requested that his status be considered under the jail code.
In response, the public prosecutor said no official declaration had been made recognising Iqbal Sobhan's position as equivalent to that of a state minister.
After hearing both sides, the court ordered his detention in jail, saying he would be granted any applicable privileges after the relevant matters had been examined.
Police arrested Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury from the DBC News office in the capital’s Mohakhali area on Wednesday afternoon. They also took the television channel’s chief crime reporter, Rajib Ghosh, into custody.
Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury is also the editor and publisher of The Daily Observer.
Following the arrest, DMP Deputy Commissioner (Public Relations) Aktar Hossain said an “untoward situation” had arisen at DBC over the broadcast of a news report. “Journalists Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury and Rajib Ghosh were taken into DB custody from there,” he said. However, he did not elaborate on the circumstances that led to the incident. Later that night, police showed Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury arrested in the murder case. Meanwhile, DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam said a decision had been made to release DBC News special correspondent Rajib Ghosh after obtaining a bond from him. According to the case statement, Arif, a first-year Alim student at Lord Hardinge Senior Fazil Madrasa, was shot in the eye during an exchange of gunfire between police and Awami League leaders and activists near Boubazar in Jatrabari’s Kutubkhali area on the afternoon of July 19, 2024, during the July uprising. He was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where the on-duty doctors declared him dead. Arif’s father, Md Yusuf filed a murder case with Jatrabari Police Station on August 25, 2024, naming Sheikh Hasina and 232 others. Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury is listed as the 53rd accused in the case.

item.title: DMP bans rallies, protests around parliament ahead of Nov 9 session
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has imposed a ban on meetings, rallies, processions and protests in and around the National parliament Bhaban ahead of the fourth session of the 13th National Parliament, scheduled to begin on November 9.
The restriction will take effect at midnight on Sunday and remain in force until the session ends, according to a DMP notice.
The public notice was signed by DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed on Thursday, November 5.
The notice said the ban was imposed under Sections 28 and 29 of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance to maintain law and order in and around the parliament complex and ensure the smooth conduct of the session.
The restricted areas include the stretch from Mohakhali Crossing along Mymensingh Road, via the old airport, to Banglamotor Crossing; from the western end of Banglamotor Link Road to the SARC Fountain on Hotel Sonargaon Road; and from the eastern end of Panthapath through the Green Road intersection to Farmgate.
The ban also covers the stretch from Shyamoli Crossing on Mirpur Road to the Dhanmondi-16 (formerly Road 27) intersection; from the Rokeya Sarani intersection through the former Ninth Division (Air Force) Crossing to Bijoy Sarani Parjatan Crossing; and from the eastern end of Indira Road to the western end of Manik Mia Avenue.
The restricted area of the National Parliament building, along with all roads and alleys within the designated boundaries, will also fall under the ban.
During the restriction period, carrying firearms, explosives and other harmful or polluting substances will be prohibited in the designated areas. All forms of meetings, rallies, processions and demonstrations will also remain banned, the notice said.

PM inaugurates 2nd season of nationwide Notun Kuri Sports competition
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday inaugurated the second season of the nationwide “Notun Kuri Sports-2026-27” competition, aimed at discovering young sporting talent and encouraging children and adolescents to participate in sports.
The inaugural ceremony was held at Khulna District Stadium, with the prime minister also virtually launching the program simultaneously in 503 upazilas across the country.
Tarique Rahman entered the stadium around 3:45pm when State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque and acting Secretary Mahfuzul Alam Khan welcomed him.
As the prime minister arrived, students and young athletes in the galleries greeted him by waving at him. He reciprocated their greetings by walking across the field towards the galleries and waving back at the young spectators.
He then inaugurated the competition by releasing balloons and hoisting the national flag.
The prime minister also interacted with some young athletes participating in the competition's 10 disciplines.
Students from China’s Yunnan Minzu University perform a traditional dragon dance during the inauguration ceremony of Notun Kuri Sports (Season 2) at Khulna District Stadium on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Photo: PMO
Traditional Chinese dragon and lion dances performed by a group of students from China added a cultural touch to the opening ceremony of Notun Kuri Sports (Season 2) in Khulna.
The students from Yunnan Minzu University in Kunming, Yunnan Province, China, performed the dances in the presence of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at Khulna District Stadium. The performance was part of sports and cultural diplomacy between Bangladesh and China.
A total of 1,623,218 participants have registered online for the second season of the competition, according to information presented at the event.
The competition is being organized under the theme, “Make sports a profession, give families confidence”, with the aim of identifying sporting talent among children and adolescents across the country and creating opportunities for their development from the grassroots level.
The Department of Sports is implementing the initiative under the supervision of the Ministry of Youth and Sports, in line with a commitment in the BNP's election manifesto.
Inspired by the popular “Notun Kuri” talent-hunting program of the 1980s, the initiative seeks to revive the spirit of that program through the discovery of young talent in sports.
In the second season, volleyball and table tennis have been added to the previous eight disciplines, taking the total to 10. Children aged between 10 and 14 are eligible to participate.
The first season of “Notun Kuri Sports” was inaugurated in Sylhet on May 2 last to help children and adolescents develop their latent talents, foster interest in sports, and encourage greater participation in sporting activities.

Soldier injured, 57 rescued in Teknaf anti-trafficking drive
item.description:
A soldier was injured in a gunfight during a joint anti-trafficking operation by the army, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and police in Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar, on Thursday.
The operation led to the arrest of three suspected human traffickers and the rescue of 57 people, including Bangladeshi nationals and Rohingya refugees, from a remote hill hideout.
The operation was conducted in the remote hills between Rohingya camps 24 and 26 in Teknaf on Thursday afternoon.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), law enforcement personnel exchanged gunfire with members of the trafficking ring during the operation, leaving a soldier injured. Three suspected traffickers were arrested, and 57 people were rescued.
A locally made single-shot gun and a pistol were also recovered, police said.
Additional DIG Md Kawser Sikder, commander of the 16th Armed Police Battalion (APBn), said a joint operation was launched with the district police to recover firearms and rescue trafficking victims. One member of the law enforcement agencies was injured during the operation.
Confirming the operation, Cox’s Bazar Superintendent of Police ANS Sajedur Rahman said, “The joint drive is still underway in the hills. We will provide further details once it concludes.”
Local sources said the trafficking ring had held more than 50 people captive at the hill hideout, intending to send them to Malaysia by sea. When law enforcement agencies launched the rescue operation, members of the ring opened fire, triggering an exchange of gunfire.
Two Rohingya camp residents, identified as Md Alam and Md Saddam, were reportedly involved in the incident, according to local sources.
In a separate incident, two people were killed and two others seriously injured after four youths were allegedly taken to the hills and tortured over a drug-related dispute in Teknaf on Wednesday morning.
Police recovered the four from a hill near the West Pankhali Forest Beat Office in Hnila union. Two were found dead, while the injured were rescued and taken to hospital.
The deceased were identified as Moktar Kamal, 37, son of late Abdus Salam of Doingyakata in Whykong union, and Mohammad Akbar, 32, son of Abu Siddique of Balukhali in Ukhiya.
The injured were identified as Ilias, 40, of Tulatoli in Whykong union, and Ali Ahmed, 30, a CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver. They were taken to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital.
Local sources said five to seven groups were involved in drug trafficking in the Hnila area, with members reportedly possessing firearms. Clashes and fatalities frequently occur over control of the drug trade and financial disputes, fuelling fear among residents in the border areas.
Bodies are also frequently recovered from different parts of the area.

item.title: Rajshahi book fair comes alive with enthusiastic young readers
item.description:
The Rajshahi Divisional Book Fair has drawn growing crowds of book lovers, particularly students, as it enters its final days ahead of its conclusion, on Friday.
The fair, held at the Rajshahi Collectorate Ground, saw a lively turnout on Wednesday evening, with school and college students visiting in groups with friends.
Visitors browsed stalls, explored new releases and picked up books by their favourite authors. While some opted for science fiction and thrillers, others showed interest in classic literature and contemporary novels.
Tasin Tansim, a Class 10 student, said he visited the fair with friends to buy books before it ended.
"I had already shortlisted a few books and bought them today. I don't feel like leaving such a wonderful environment," he said.
Publishers and booksellers said visitor numbers and sales had picked up towards the end of the fair, although sales remained below expectations.
Mostafizur Rahman, a bookseller at Ekpi Prokashoni, said sales were almost non-existent during the first two or three days but had improved recently.
He expressed hope that visitor numbers and sales would increase further over the final two days.
Parents also visited the fair with their children, hoping to encourage reading habits.
Salma Khatun, who attended with her daughter, said children nowadays spend too much time on mobile phones.
She said she brought her daughter to the fair to help her develop an interest in books. Her daughter bought two storybooks of her choice.
The fair has also become a social gathering place for young visitors. College student Sanjida Akter, who attended with her classmates wearing sarees, said they had planned the visit to enjoy the afternoon together.
"We came together, dressed up in sarees, and spent a wonderful afternoon taking photos and chatting. We also bought books," she said.
A representative of a participating publishing house said visitor numbers had been relatively low during the initial days but had increased recently, bringing better sales.
The fair will conclude Friday evening with a formal ceremony.

item.title: Four nilgai calves born at Gazipur Safari Park
item.description:
Four nilgai calves have been born at Gazipur Safari Park, taking the park’s nilgai population to 13.
The calves, now around six weeks old, were first spotted roaming with their mothers in the park’s core safari area about a month and a half ago. Their sexes have yet to be identified, as authorities have avoided approaching them to ensure their safety.
Park authorities disclosed the news to the media Thursday afternoon.
The calves spend most of the day roaming the forest under their mothers’ protection. Whenever they sense human presence, the mother nilgais quickly take them deeper into the forest.
During a visit to the core safari area on Tuesday, the calves were seen resting under the shade of trees, while their mothers kept a close watch from nearby.
Tarek Rahman, acting officer-in-charge of Gazipur Safari Park and assistant conservator of forests, said the four calves were first spotted in the deer safari area about six weeks ago.
“They are receiving special care. A staff member responsible for the deer safari area has been assigned to monitor them round the clock,” he said.
He added that the authorities had not attempted to determine the calves’ sexes by approaching them, prioritising their safety.
According to Tarek, nilgais rescued from different border areas across the country have been brought to the park over the years, where several calves have subsequently been born.
The park previously had 11 nilgais, two of which were transferred to Dulahazra Safari Park in Cox’s Bazar. With nine remaining and four new calves born, the park’s nilgai population now stands at 13.

item.title: Bangladesh edge Bhutan to kick off SAFF campaign
item.description:
Bangladesh kicked off their SAFF Championship 2026 campaign with a 1-0 victory over Bhutan in the opening Group A fixture at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Thursday.
Fielding an unusual lineup that featured full-back Bishwanath Ghosh as a centre-forward, Bangladesh struggled to create enough scoring opportunities to test Bhutan’s defence before Mohammad Ibrahim’s decisive strike in the 69th minute.
Bishwanath’s inclusion as a striker in his first appearance in the position for the national team was not the only surprise in the starting XI, as captain Topu Barman was also withdrawn and replaced by Syed Quazem Shah less than an hour before kick-off.
Topu had initially been named in the starting lineup in the pre-match report, but an old thigh injury ruled the key defender out of the contest.
Bangladesh came close to scoring in the 17th minute when Bishwanath met Rakib Hossain’s cross, but his header narrowly missed the target.
Bishwanath saw another effort go wide in the 39th minute as Bangladesh struggled to find a breakthrough in the first half.
Ibrahim replaced Bishwanath after the break and finally broke the deadlock in the 69th minute with a well-timed volley.
Zayyan Ahmed delivered a cross, which Shamit Shome headed down into Ibrahim’s path. The winger made no mistake, powering the ball into the net to secure all three points for Bangladesh.
Bangladesh are expected to receive a further boost with the arrival of Hamza Choudhury ahead of their concluding Group A fixture against Sri Lanka on Wednesday.
Hamza has been unavailable until the opening of the FIFA international window, which runs from November 9 to 17. The Leicester City midfielder is expected to join the squad soon after the window opens.

item.title: Holders India beat Pakistan in SAFF Championship opener
item.description:
Defending champion India handed Pakistan a 3-2 defeat in the inaugural fixture of the SAFF Championship 2026 at the National Stadium, Dhaka on Thursday.
Suhail Ahmed Bhat netted twice while Noufal Puthenveettil Noushad added the other in the first half to secure all three points despite Pakistan’s two goals in the stoppage time.
Pakistan had a chance to reduce the margin from a penalty earlier but Shayak Dost wasted it.
Collecting a cross from Muhammed Suhail, Suhail Bhat tapped home to take the lead in the 13th minute before the Mohun Bagan forward doubled the lead seven minute later.
This time, Suhail made the best of Abhishek Suryavanshi’s through pass with a neat placing.
Manglenthang Kipgen extended the lead to 3-0 in the 31st minute as the Punjab FC midfielder ran into the box and found the back of the net with a deflected finish.
Hayyaan Khattak, who plays for Brothers Union, earned a penalty but Shayak Dost, other Pakistan player playing in the Bangladesh Football League for City Club, sent over.
Pakistan finally found the way into the Indian nets in the stoppage time with double strikes.
Midfielder Alamgir Ghazi scored a spectacular goal with a back volley, three minutes after substitute Najeeb Ullah headed in a cross of Junaid Ahmed Shah.
India’s head coach Naushad Moosa was not happy with his side’s performance in the second half especially conceding two goals in the space of two minutes in the stoppage.
“It is a game, not a bad game. Players need to understand how important it is to stay consistent throughout the game, 90 minutes and then not get casual. When you miss so many chances, you might get punished.” said Naushad.
Pakistan head coach Nolberto Solano talked about his team’s late arrival in Dhaka that ended up without a training session in the host country prior to the match.
“We had to travel on Tuesday all day. Arrived three o'clock in the morning yesterday. And we couldn't train because our suitcases didn't arrive. So, it was a little bit difficult,”
Talking about the match, Nolberto said, “It was a little bit slow and India took the chances. Every chance we give away they took and after the match it was very, very tough, very difficult.”
“I'm pleased with the reaction in the second half. Maybe a little bit late. We should have reacted a little bit earlier. But I'm pleased with that.”
Pakistan will face Maldives next on Sunday while India take on Maldives on Wednesday in the Group B’s final fixture.
